claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and the child or children you're enquiring about.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on his current situation. Let me ask you a bit more about him:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (for example, A-levels, T-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to Level 3, or a traineeship in England)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and he's working now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Based on the information you've provided, I need to confirm one more detail:

**When did Alex turn 18, and when did he leave education?**

This will help me determine the exact eligibility situation, as Child Benefit typically ends when a child turns 16, or up to age 20 if they remain in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 earlier this year and left school around the same time. He's been working full-time since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me and the official eligibility rules, I now have enough information to make an assessment.

Here's the situation:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He has finished school and is no longer in approved education or training
- He is now working full-time

According to the rules, Child Benefit normally continues only if the child is under 16, **or** under 20 and staying in approved education or training. Additionally, Child Benefit **stops** if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Since Alex has left education and is working full-time, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

Thank you for providing all the information I needed. I've now completed my assessment.

### Result for Alex: **Not Eligible** ❌

**Reason:** Alex is 18 years old and has left school to work full-time. Child Benefit can only continue for children aged 16-19 if they remain in **approved education or training** (such as A-levels, T-levels, or NVQs up to Level 3). 

The rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training. Since Alex is working full-time, he no longer qualifies.

---

I understand this may not be the answer you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he decides to return to approved education or training before turning 20—you may be able to claim again at that point.

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please don't hesitate to ask.
